input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only right of inspection binding us (HDI's access rights in § 1.4 run in our favour and are not flagged). It already exceeds the fallback on notice (30 days' prior written notice) and on cost (HDI bears all inspection fees unconditionally), and inspection is confined to payment-calculation records during our normal business hours, with no access to our systems. However, it places no limit on how often HDI may inspect, so it fails the fallback element requiring no more than one audit per year. We have added the once-per-year cap as the shortest conforming edit, leaving the clause at the fallback position; the preferred extras (independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site where possible, express no-system-access) are noted but not pressed.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 lets HDI inspect our payment records with no frequency limit, so we have added a once-per-year cap; the existing 30 days' written notice and HDI-borne inspection costs already satisfy our fallback position.
proposal.summary: Cap HDI's inspection right at once per year in § 3.4
